why: CI-only fix, Tier-1 by the canonical doc's own list. The whole diff is one workflow file (.github/workflows/research-loss-detector.yml) plus one docs/claude/work/pipeline/ record filing an unrelated finding -- no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no unit file, no order path, no strategy/risk/sizing value touched. Root cause verified independently by reading the file and reproducing the shell behavior locally (not just trusting the dispatching manager's diagnosis): GitHub Actions runs `run:` steps as `bash -eo pipefail`, so the step's own `set -uo pipefail` (no `e`) never clears the runner's `-e`. When scripts/ops/research_loss_detector.py exits 1 (findings) or 2 (could-not-read) -- both documented, intended answers, not errors -- the `python3 ... | tee ...` pipe fails under pipefail+e and aborts the step before `rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is captured, so `steps.detect.outputs.rc` is empty and the 'Land the receipt on main' step (gated on `rc != ''`) is skipped on every such run. Confirmed against the actual failed runs (36097174392, 36166465663, 36219983517) and against docs/claude/work/RESEARCH-LOSS-RECEIPT.json's ~40h-stale age, which is exactly what check_cadence_liveness.py grades STALE and fails on `guards` for every open PR. Fix wraps only the risky pipe in a scoped `set +e` / `set -e`, matching the identical, already-fixed bug shape in .github/workflows/oci-inventory.yml (its own header: 'THE POSITIVE CONTROL FOUND A REAL DEFECT') -- deliberately placed around just the detector pipe rather than immediately after `set -uo pipefail` for the whole step, so `git fetch --no-tags origin main` earlier in the same step keeps its fail-fast behavior instead of silently swallowing a fetch failure too. Swept every other workflow for the same shape (`set -uo pipefail` + PIPESTATUS-into-GITHUB_OUTPUT): 66 files use `set -uo pipefail`, 3 also capture PIPESTATUS (oci-inventory.yml, research-loss-detector.yml, trainer-capture-watch.yml). oci-inventory.yml is already fixed (positive control). trainer-capture-watch.yml's `grade` step has the identical live bug -- its `continue-on-error: true` stops the JOB from failing but does not let the aborted script continue past the pipe, so its stale-capture/broken-controls paging steps never fire in exactly the case the alarm exists to catch. Filed as PI-20260926-P64CTNIO-0001 rather than fixed here, to keep this PR to the one workflow the guards failure is actually about. No parameter, roster or execution value is changed anywhere in this diff.
